name: Republic of Colombia

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 1,140,619 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 1,109,500 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes the San Andres archipelago.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 53,425,635). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:COL.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.417 as quoted: 285,000 active (excludes 165,050 paramilitary National Police). CIA Factbook 2025: ~260,000 active Military Forces (low). World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 428,000 (2020) includes police.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 34,950 reserves. High is an educated allowance for recently discharged conscripts.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 285,000 (IISS 2026) minus infantry P roles (2,000 + 140,000). Covers navy (~35,000 incl. marines counted partly in P roles), air force (~13,000), army aviation, engineers, logistics, staff and static-security garrisons.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to states with long internal wars and conscription: Colombia sustains ~285,000 active plus 165,000 police from 53 million (0.85%); total war could plausibly reach WWII-belligerent lower bounds. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized cavalry/infantry squadrons on LAV III, M1117 and Urutu; Colombia has almost no mechanized infantry. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_National_Army_of_Colombia)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: LAV III modern, rest old.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: six decades of counter-insurgency make it one of the most combat-experienced armies in the hemisphere; conscript (soldado regular/bachiller) share discounts.

count.note: Educated guess. Counter-guerrilla, high-mountain, jungle and special-forces battalions (~200 battalion-sized units, many static security) plus ~22,000 marines (Colombian Navy article, 2013). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_Navy)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Galil ACE/Tavor, Spike ATGMs, abundant helicopter mobility.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: six decades of counter-insurgency make it one of the most combat-experienced armies in the hemisphere; conscript (soldado regular/bachiller) share discounts.

count.note: Equipment list: LAV III 82 + EE-9 Cascavel 121 + M113A2 28 (up to 60 more stored) + EE-11 Urutu 100 + M1117 87 + Sand Cat 22 + RG-31 4 + ISBI Meteoro 16 = 460. No tanks: armor role omitted.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: mostly armoured cars and 1970s APCs; LAV III modern.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: six decades of counter-insurgency make it one of the most combat-experienced armies in the hemisphere; conscript (soldado regular/bachiller) share discounts.

count.note: Equipment list: Santa Barbara 155/52 15 + LG-1 105 mm 20 + M101 105 mm 75 = 110 tubes >=105 mm. Mortars and M116 75 mm excluded; no MLRS.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: six decades of counter-insurgency make it one of the most combat-experienced armies in the hemisphere; conscript (soldado regular/bachiller) share discounts.

count.note: Colombian Aerospace Force inventory: IAI Kfir 16, phasing out; 17 JAS 39 Gripen E/F on order (first deliveries expected from 2026, high).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: Kfir C10/C12 with Python 5/Derby and EL/M-2032 radar, but an old airframe.

count.note: EMB 314 Super Tucano 24 + Basler AC-47T gunships 6 = 30.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: COIN turboprops with precision munitions.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: very high operational tempo against FARC/ELN, precision-strike experience.

count.note: Air Force: Bell 212 11 + UH-1 52 + UH-60L/AH-60 24 + MD 530 4 = 91 (Bell 206 trainers excluded). Army aviation: UH-1H/N 64 + Mi-17 20 + UH-60L/S-70i 60 = 144 (Army equipment list). Navy: ~12 (Colombian Navy article). Total ~247; one of the largest Black Hawk fleets in Latin America.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Black Hawk family dominant, armed AH-60L Arpia.

count.note: Air Force: ScanEagle 6 + Hermes 450 6 + Hermes 900 2 = 14; mid/high add Navy ScanEagle and Army systems (educated). RQ-11 Ravens excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: MALE ISR, some armed use claimed.

count.note: Active ships list: Almirante Padilla-class (FS-1500) missile frigates 4, upgraded 2012; SIGMA 10514 replacements from 2026-2030.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: 1983-84 light frigates with Exocet; modest air defence.

count.note: Active ships list: Fassmer OPVs 4 (incl. 24 de Julio delivered Jan 2026) + ex-ROK Pohang/Donghae corvettes 2 + CPV coastal patrol 4 + riverine motherships ~10 + heavy river gunboats ~3 + amphibious/landing craft; mid ~30.
Active ships list: Type 209/1200 2 (1975) + Type 206A 2 (ex-German, 2015) = 4. Low allows for refits.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: old boats, upgraded.

count.note: Equipment list: mainly towed AA guns (some in reserve) and ~60 FIM-92 Stinger; no SAM batteries. Counted as a handful of batteries (educated conversion).

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: combat-proven joint command from the FARC war (Plan Colombia, Operation Jaque), US-trained staff; little conventional interstate experience.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional soldiers (soldados profesionales) with strong unit identity; scandals (false positives) and politicization strain.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: motivated by long internal war; border tension with Venezuela.

weapons.note: Near anchor 9: Spike ATGMs, precision-guided bombs on Super Tucano, Kfir with Derby BVR; no long-range fires.

armor.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: no tanks; LAV III and MRAPs.

ships.note: Near anchor 9: 1980s frigates, Type 209/206 submarines, modern OPVs built by Cotecmar.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: hardened bases against insurgent attack; no layered air defence.

logistics.note: Near anchor 9: large helicopter/airlift fleet (C-130, C-295, KC-767), weak road/rail network.

communications.note: Anchor 9: Link-Colombia data links, US/NATO interoperability; no military satellite.

isr.note: Anchor 9: Hermes 900/450, ScanEagle, intelligence fusion from counter-insurgency, FACSAT small satellites.

air.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Kfir fleet; Gripen E/F only from 2026.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 803,110,596,926 / population 53,425,635 = 15,032 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 1,003,261,207,903 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 803,110,596,926 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/COL/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 3.20% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 3.0% (2022-23), 3.4% (2024); includes the National Police budget under the Ministry of Defence.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 21.76% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.15 -> 0.81. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/COL/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 14.16% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.76 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.76-0.76). Mid 1 - 0.142/0.76 = 0.81. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.76 = 0.76. High: s 0.76 = 0.81. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 76% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Exports coffee, flowers, bananas, palm oil but imports most cereals; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 26,358,472 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 7.569% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 399,028. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Cotecmar Cartagena builds OPVs, coastal and riverine patrol vessels; SIGMA frigate programme from 2026. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_ships_of_the_Colombian_Navy)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Hunter TR-12 light armoured vehicle in local production (Army equipment list). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_National_Army_of_Colombia)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 204,389 km total (2021), 32,280 km paved, 172,109 km unpaved, 2,100 km controlled-access. Mid is paved plus half the unpaved network (derived midpoint); high is the total.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 2,141 km (2019), mostly 914 mm narrow gauge, much of it disused. World Bank has no value.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 14 ports, 0 large + 2 medium + 8 small; key ports Cartagena, Barranquilla, Santa Marta, Buenaventura (named). Mid counts those four.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Colombia is below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-fleet table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country); CIA Factbook 2023 counts 153 merchant ships (28 general cargo, 13 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Mountain and jungle terrain; operations sustained by helicopter and river transport.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys (roughly 1.5 million horses plus mules); not from FAO data. Mule trains still used in mountain operations.

nuclearWarheads.note: Colombia is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Party to Tlatelolco.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: three Andean cordilleras, jungle and population support; high 1.3 for terrain an invader is not adapted to (Darien, Amazon).

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:COL (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2026 (personnel) as quoted; Army equipment list, Colombian Aerospace Force inventory and the active ships list of the Colombian Navy. No tanks: armor role omitted. ships_major = frigates; ships_minor = OPVs, corvettes, coastal/riverine patrol; drones = Group 2+ UAVs. Infantry P-role split is an educated guess (grade D): the army is overwhelmingly light infantry and much of it is tied to internal security against ELN and FARC dissidents. National Police (165,050) excluded.
